f01.title: What law does
f01.summary: Law supplies public standards, institutions, procedures and remedies for organizing power and resolving disputes.
f01.eli15: Think of law as a shared rulebook plus referees, proof rules and ways to fix a wrong.

f02.title: Facts, law, evidence and argument
f02.summary: Separate what happened, the rule that governs it, the material that can prove it, and the reason offered for a result.
f02.eli15: A fact is the event, evidence is how you show it, law is the rule, and argument connects them.

f03.title: Public law, private law, civil law and criminal law
f03.summary: These classifications identify who is acting, whose interests are protected, the process used and the possible consequences.
f03.eli15: Ask who is fighting whom, why the state is involved, and what can happen at the end.

f04.title: Legal actors and institutions
f04.summary: Map legislatures, executives, courts, tribunals, police, regulators, lawyers, parties, witnesses and enforcement officers.
f04.eli15: Every legal problem has players. First learn who can make, apply, challenge and enforce a rule.

f05.title: Sources and hierarchy of authority
f05.summary: Distinguish constitutions, statutes, delegated legislation, precedent, custom, treaties, soft law and persuasive material.
f05.eli15: Not every rule has the same rank. A lower rule cannot normally defeat a higher one.

f06.title: Anatomy of a statute
f06.summary: Read title, purpose, extent, commencement, definitions, operative rules, provisos, explanations, schedules and amendment history.
f06.eli15: A statute is engineered. Its definitions and exceptions can change what an ordinary word means.

f07.title: Anatomy of a judgment
f07.summary: Identify court, posture, material facts, issues, holdings, reasons, orders, separate opinions and later treatment.
f07.eli15: The important part is not who won alone, but the rule the court used and why.

f08.title: Ratio, obiter and precedent
f08.summary: Work out what proposition was necessary to decide the case, what was additional, and how court hierarchy affects force.
f08.eli15: A case is binding for the rule needed to decide it, not every sentence in the judgment.

f09.title: Jurisdiction, forum and maintainability
f09.summary: Before merits, ask whether the decision-maker has territorial, subject, personal and procedural authority to act.
f09.eli15: Even a strong claim can fail in the wrong court or through the wrong procedure.

f10.title: Legal persons, status and capacity
f10.summary: Law attributes rights, duties, powers and disabilities to natural persons, groups, corporations, states and institutions.
f10.eli15: Law decides who counts as a legal person and what each person is allowed to do.

f11.title: Rights, duties, powers, liberties and liabilities
f11.summary: Use Hohfeldian relations to avoid treating every legal advantage as the same kind of right.
f11.eli15: Your right may mean someone owes you a duty, or simply that you are free to act. Those are different.

f12.title: Elements, tests, exceptions and defences
f12.summary: Turn a doctrine into a checklist, then identify exclusions, burdens, standards and consequences for each element.
f12.eli15: Most legal rules work like a recipe: required ingredients, special exceptions and a result.

f13.title: Burdens, standards and presumptions
f13.summary: Distinguish legal and evidential burdens, standards of proof, rebuttable presumptions and adverse inferences.
f13.eli15: Ask who must prove what, how convincing the proof must be, and what the law assumes at the start.

f14.title: Lifecycle of a legal dispute
f14.summary: Trace intake, cause of action or offence, forum, pleadings or charge, interim relief, proof, decision, appeal and enforcement.
f14.eli15: A dispute moves through stages. A rule can matter at one stage and be irrelevant at another.

f15.title: Remedies and enforcement
f15.summary: Compare compensation, restitution, injunction, declaration, specific performance, punishment, judicial review and institutional orders.
f15.eli15: Winning means little unless the legal system can give and enforce the right kind of fix.

f16.title: Interpretation and legal reasoning
f16.summary: Use text, context, purpose, precedent, principle, analogy and consequence while respecting institutional limits.
f16.eli15: Legal reading is not guessing what feels fair; it is giving reasons that fit the legal materials.

f17.title: Fact chronology and issue tree
f17.summary: Build a dated fact map, identify disputed facts, and decompose the legal question into nested issues.
f17.eli15: Put events in order, then turn one big problem into smaller questions you can answer.

f18.title: Legal research and source verification
f18.summary: Move from secondary orientation to primary authority, verify currency, history, jurisdiction and later treatment.
f18.eli15: Do not stop at the first summary. Find the real rule, check that it is current, and see whether later law changed it.

f19.title: Rule synthesis and IRAC
f19.summary: Synthesize multiple authorities into a usable rule and apply it to each material fact before reaching a conclusion.
f19.eli15: State the question, give the rule, connect each fact to the rule, and then answer.

f20.title: Legal writing and citation
f20.summary: Write propositions with authority, distinguish fact from inference, use headings, and cite sources so a reader can verify them.
f20.eli15: Make each important claim easy to understand and easy to check.

f21.title: Client interviewing and counselling
f21.summary: Elicit facts without leading, explain options and risk, identify objectives, obtain instructions and preserve confidentiality.
f21.eli15: Listen first, ask clear questions, explain choices honestly, and let the client decide.

f22.title: Negotiation and settlement thinking
f22.summary: Separate positions from interests, assess alternatives, generate options and test enforceable settlement terms.
f22.eli15: Work out what each side really needs and what happens if no deal is made.

f23.title: Drafting rules and instruments
f23.summary: Draft for legal effect, defined terms, conditions, allocation of risk, procedure, remedies and predictable interpretation.
f23.eli15: Good drafting tells people exactly who must do what, when, and what happens if they do not.

f24.title: Oral advocacy and response
f24.summary: Lead with the requested order and decisive issue, answer the question asked, use the record, and concede safely where needed.
f24.eli15: Tell the decision-maker what you need, why the law permits it, and where the facts prove it.

f25.title: Professional responsibility and confidentiality
f25.summary: Identify duties to client, court, opponent, profession and public; manage conflicts, candour, competence, money and confidential information.
f25.eli15: A lawyer serves a client but cannot lie to the court, misuse trust or ignore conflicts.

f26.title: Current-law and edition check
f26.summary: Check commencement, amendments, repeals, replacement codes, rules, notifications and binding decisions as of the research date.
f26.eli15: A perfect note on old law is still wrong today. Always check what is now in force.
